answer: Whether an agent buys velvet, books a jetty berth, or orders a sparrow census, the marketplace requires each bidding identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days. Creating aliases is cheap, but activating 1,000 bidders ties up $100,000 for a month. Funds cannot back multiple identities at once, so an attacker seeking to flood auctions with fake participants must supply capital in direct proportion to the number of active aliases.
